labels.fast_path_mutate: A single, specific calendar or reminder mutation the coordinator can execute directly after conflict checks: create, update, move, delete, or restore an event, or draft/cancel a reminder, for one clear family and activity. Pending parent approval before the mutating tool call.
labels.fast_path_read: A single, specific read-only request: list or show existing events, reminders, or activities for a family, child, or date range. No mutation, no approval gate.
labels.fast_path_reject: A single, specific request that must be declined outright by deterministic safeguards: a past-dated event, a direct child/parent/transportation conflict, cross-family access, a stale plan version, or an unsafe retry after a prior rejection.
labels.deep_weekly_workflow: A broad, multi-day coordination request needing the full specialist pipeline (intake, weekly planner, transportation, schedule reviewer, reminder agent) to check school and family calendars, resolve conflicts, and produce a reviewed weekly plan.
labels.outing_workflow: A request for cited outing or activity ideas for a weekend or school break, routed to the Family Outing Agent's constrained search wrapper. Never mutates the calendar.
labels.ambiguous_clarify: A request missing information the coordinator needs before acting (which event, which family, which time) and must be answered with a clarifying question rather than a tool call.

manual_expansion.note: Pass-2 finding (notebooks/finetune_family_request_router.ipynb Recap): prompt-only instructions fixed the outing_workflow/fast_path_read confusion but not the fast_path_reject / ambiguous_clarify / deep_weekly_workflow cluster. Added 48 hand-written contrastive examples for those labels (plus fast_path_mutate reinforcement) and fixed 4 fast_path_reject rows whose disqualifying fact was not actually present in the text (relied on unstated cross-family membership).

new_label_fast_path_conflict.note: Split out of fast_path_reject: scheduling conflicts (same child/parent double-booked) are a genuinely different downstream action in the Family Coordinator (offer alternatives / flag possible parent error) than an outright deterministic decline, so they now get their own routing label instead of being folded into fast_path_reject.

minimal_pair_expansion.note: Pass-4 finding (notebook Recap): ambiguous_clarify had 0% recall under every label structure tried so far, with its confusion target moving from fast_path_reject to fast_path_mutate depending on the taxonomy. Added 15 reject/clarify/mutate minimal-pair triplets (45 rows): each triplet holds the base request constant and varies exactly one fact (a stated disqualifying fact -> reject, that same fact omitted -> clarify, stated and fine -> mutate), to give the model a direct signal for this specific three-way boundary instead of relying on lexical diversity across unrelated examples.
